0.0.n: Combines with カード to name a type of game card.

0.1.n: A borrowed word; Japanese does not mark singular or plural here.

0.2.n: Casual form of という, introducing the term being explained.

0.3.n: Turns the preceding expression into something the speaker can explain.

0.4.n: Marks investigation cards as the topic.

0.5.n: Works with ように to compare these cards with something previously mentioned.

0.6.n: 同じよう means a similar manner or arrangement.

0.7.n: Makes 同じよう describe how the cards come in colors.

0.8.n: 色 counts colors here, referring to the cards' three color categories.

0.9.n: Plain form of ある, used for things rather than people.

0.10.n: Conversational shortening of ので or の Aで, linking this explanation to what follows.

0.12.n: 戦闘 means combat; 系 adds the sense of a category or type.

0.13.n: Lists an example without claiming the list is complete.

0.14.n: 外交 means diplomacy; 系 identifies cards belonging to that category.

0.15.n: Continues the open-ended list of card categories.

0.16.n: 魔法 means magic; 系 labels the corresponding category.

0.17.n: Casual という connects the listed category names to the cards being described.

0.18.n: Needs な before the noun it describes.

0.19.n: Connects 様々 to 調査カード as a description.

0.20.n: Forms the compound 調査カード with the following noun.

0.21.n: Here it refers to multiple game cards across different categories.

0.22.n: Marks 調査カード as the things that exist.

0.23.n: States that these different card types exist.

0.24.n: Gives a reason and leaves the explanation connected to the next line.

1.0.n: Refers to something already being discussed; the exact reference depends on the game context.

1.1.n: Marks これ as something acted on, although the spoken sentence is loosely structured.

1.3.n: て-form of 行く, connecting going somewhere with the next action.

1.4.n: 何とかする loosely stands in for doing whatever the game requires.

1.5.n: する becomes したら to express a condition or an action completed before the next step.

1.6.n: Directly modifies the following noun, unlike standalone これ.

1.7.n: Refers to the investigation card the player will draw.

1.8.n: Marks このカード as what the player draws.

1.9.n: Polite suggestion form of 引く, used here to present a game instruction.

1.10.n: Quotation marker framing the preceding instruction as what the rules say.

2.0.n: 枚 counts thin, flat objects such as cards.

2.1.n: Combines with カード to identify the card type.

2.2.n: The object marker を is omitted after this noun in casual speech.

2.3.n: Ability form of 引く; the speaker literally says being able to draw a card.

2.4.n: Introduces what follows from being able to draw the card.

2.6.n: First half of どこどこ, a placeholder for an unspecified place name.

2.7.n: Repeats どこ to complete the placeholder どこどこ, rather than asking two questions.

2.8.n: Marks the destination of 行ったら.

2.9.n: 行く becomes 行ったら, setting a condition for receiving the reward.

2.10.n: Stands in for an unspecified reward rather than meaning somehow here.

2.11.n: Polite form of もらえる, expressing the possibility of getting a reward.

2.12.n: Adds an informing or reassuring tone to the example card text.

2.13.n: Together with the following か, forms とか to introduce an example.

2.14.n: Completes とか; it does not mark a question here.

2.15.n: Part of ですね, a polite conversational pause after the example.

2.16.n: Softens the explanation and invites the listener to follow along.

2.18.n: Describes the range of events written on the cards.

2.19.n: Connects 様々 to the noun イベント.

2.20.n: A borrowed word referring to game situations or tasks here.

2.21.n: Marks イベント as what is written on the cards.

2.22.n: Passive 書かれる plus ている describes text already written and present on the cards.

2.23.n: Connects the card contents as a reason for the explanation that follows.

3.0.n: Refers back to the examples of events just described.

3.1.n: Refers to the tasks or situations presented on investigation cards.

3.2.n: Marks イベント as what players work through.

3.3.n: こなす means handling tasks; ていく adds continued progress through them.

3.4.n: The preceding action describes which process the speaker means.

3.5.n: Marks the process as the setting in which the final mission is achieved.

3.7.n: Uses の to describe the mission that comes at the end.

3.8.n: Connects 最後 with 任務.

3.9.n: Refers to the game's ultimate objective or quest.

3.10.n: Marks 任務 as what players accomplish.

3.11.n: 達成する means accomplishing an objective; ていく presents this as progression over time.

3.12.n: Introduces the preceding description as the content of the overall game pattern.

3.13.n: Here よう refers to how the game unfolds, not resemblance to something else.

3.14.n: Links よう to なります to describe the resulting arrangement.

3.15.n: Polite form of なる, rounding off the explanation of how the game works.

3.16.n: Softens the conclusion and seeks shared understanding.

0.lit: Investigation cards, similarly, come in three colors, since there are various investigation cards called combat-type, diplomacy-type, and magic-type.
0.tip: っていうのは is a conversational way to introduce a term and explain what it is.

1.lit: This, go somewhere and do something, then let's draw this card, it says.
1.tip: したら sets the condition for the instruction 引きましょう: do the required action, then draw a card.

2.lit: When you can draw one investigation card, various events are written, like: go to such-and-such place and receive something, so…
2.tip: どこどこ and 何とか stand in for specific place names and rewards in the speaker's example.

3.lit: In the process of working through these events, it becomes such that you go on to accomplish the final mission.
3.tip: ていく presents completing events and achieving the mission as progress unfolding over time.
